questions.stem: What ion do all acids produce when dissolved in water?
questions.explanation: All acids produce H⁺ ions (hydrogen ions) when dissolved in water. It is the presence of these H⁺ ions that gives acids their characteristic properties.

questions.stem: What is the chemical formula of sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Sulfuric acid has the formula H₂SO₄. HCl is hydrochloric acid, HNO₃ is nitric acid, and CH₃COOH is ethanoic (acetic) acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a property of acids?

options.text: They have a pH greater than 7
They turn blue litmus paper red
They produce OH⁻ ions in solution

questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus paper red. They have a pH less than 7, taste sour (though you should never taste chemicals), and produce H⁺ ions in solution.

questions.stem: Which acid is commonly found in the human stomach?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is produced in the stomach to help digest food and kill bacteria. It gives the stomach a pH of about 1-2.

questions.stem: Why do acids only show acidic properties when dissolved in water?

options.text: Water is needed for the acid molecules to ionise and release H⁺ ions
Water acts as a catalyst for acid reactions

questions.explanation: Acids need water to ionise (dissociate) and release H⁺ ions. Without water, the acid molecules remain intact and cannot produce the H⁺ ions responsible for acidic properties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common laboratory acid?
questions.explanation: Nitric acid (HNO₃) is one of the three common laboratory acids, along with hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄). Sodium hydroxide is an alkali, not an acid.

questions.stem: What type of salt does hydrochloric acid produce in reactions?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) produces chloride salts. Sulfuric acid produces sulfates, and nitric acid produces nitrates.
